reviewedPosts.text: 10/ I do wish that @camhberg and colleagues would have been a bit more mindful of these points in their paper. Technically, they caveat their conclusions & interpretations under the guise of uncertainty, but in the current febrile AI climate it is entirely predictable that their paper will be read (wrongly) by many as strong evidence that AI systems feel pain and should have moral status.

reviewedPosts.author: anilkseth
reviewedPosts.text:
9/ While @camhberg explore the ethical consequences of LLMs actually experiencing pain, they do not balance this with the ethical costs of falsely attributing conscious pain. 

Obvious problems here include (i) mental distress to human users who may worry about causing conscious pain to LLMs, and (ii) unnecessary and potentially catastrophic constraints on regulation and control intended to avoid causing  LLM pain. If avoiding LLM 'pain' conflicted with human interests, then taking LLM pain seriously would be misaligned with our interests.  

This is where I'm with @mustafasuleyman on his Humanist AI agenda (though I would add a bit more nuance: we don't know for sure that AIs are not conscious. It's just vanishingly unlikely that they are). https://t.co/jwa6g8QEUB

reviewedPosts.author: anilkseth
reviewedPosts.text: 8/ However, there are compelling arguments against computational functionalism (see, e.g., work by @gualtieropicc @De_dicto @pgodfreysmith and others, including my recent @BBSJournal paper (https://t.co/6ZFzHrV0Kp). If these arguments are on track, LLM consciousness is off the table, and so is LLM pain.
reviewedPosts.evidence: 反对计算功能主义论证

reviewedPosts.author: anilkseth
reviewedPosts.text: 7/ Second: The very possibility of conscious experiences in LLMs requires computational functionalism to be true. (This is the assumption that substrate-independent computation is sufficient for consciousness). The authors recognise that they haven't shown that LLMs are capable of consciousness, but they cite the Butlin et al paper which assumes computational functionalism to be true.

reviewedPosts.author: anilkseth
reviewedPosts.text:
6/ First: The presence of a 'pain' vector in an LLM is exactly what one would predict to happen given the data that LLMs are trained on (which involve lots of examples of pain, its causes, and its consequences). So it is not surprising that pain vectors arise and can be used to explain & steer model behaviour. There is absolutely no need for these 'pain' representations to be accompanied by conscious experiences. Since conscious 'pain' in LLMs would require additional justification - which the authors admit they haven't provided - the most parsimonious explanation is that LLMs do not in fact experience pain.  

(A similar argument applies to the recent identification of 'J-spaces' in Claude: https://t.co/nd9rXMU4L1)

reviewedPosts.text: Enjoy the read! Just to clarify, I never say "... computational functionalism [CF] is wrong. Thus, biological naturalism [BN]".  If BN is true, CF has to be false (for substrate-independent computation), but if CF is false (which I think it is), it doesn't follow that BN is true. Other non-computational theories could be true (e,g, IIT).  And for 'conscious AI' to be ruled out it is basically enough for CF to be false: BN doesn't need to be true.

Introducing DocJev - a lightning-fast OSS library for document classification and splitting with jev ⚡️

Give a document alongside some natural language category rules. Jev will predict the document category (classify) or the boundaries between sub-documents (split).

It is 6x faster than gpt-5.6-luna with equivalent accuracy.

You can choose between different OCR backends:
liteparse: the fastest/most accurate free+OSS text parser out there. Perfect for digitalized documents. The speedups vs. luna above are inclusive of liteparse times.
LlamaParse: the most advanced VLM-based solution for complex docs. Using this will of course add latency on document preprocessing. But it’s a good option if you want to cache the digitalized representations of documents for a variety of downstream tasks.

Check it out: https://t.co/PVE4hbEyFR

If you want to dive deeper into liteparse or LlamaParse check the links below:
liteparse: https://t.co/JNER0mVcB8
LlamaParse: https://t.co/XYZmx5TFz8

真挺期待多模态 Jev，尤其是能直接看屏幕的版本。

这两天的几个 Demo 已经很快了，但仔细看，Doom 喂的是游戏状态，浏览器和手机 Agent 读的是程序提取的界面元素，都需要先把环境整理成它能读的信息。

问题也在这里，屏幕上看得到、却没被提取出来的内容，Jev 就用不上。遇到图表、纯图标或自绘界面，还得额外补一层视觉理解。

如果能直接看图做决策，同时保住低延迟和低成本，Agent 就有望减少中间的信息转换，操作更连贯，也更少依赖应用提供的界面结构。

最期待看到的，是这种速度能延续到陌生、复杂的真实界面里。那对电脑和手机 Agent 的实用性，应该会是很实在的一步。

reviewedPosts.author: Xudong07452910
reviewedPosts.text:
我们一直在研究怎么让 Agent 更聪明。

这篇论文反过来问了一句：

能不能让 Agent 自己研究，怎么把自己跑得更便宜？

NVIDIA、NTU、MIT 团队的 SoL-Pi，就是让 Research Agent 自动发现 Harness 里的 Token 浪费，再通过大规模实验筛掉无效改法。

他们让 Research Agent 观察真实执行轨迹，提出 Harness 改法，再放进大量环境中反复测试。整个搜索覆盖 152 个方向、535 个可执行环境和 3000+ 次实验。

最后真正留下来的只有 4 个机制。

思路其实还挺朴素的：合并连续工具操作；只在划算的时候压缩上下文；大段工具输出先存起来、需要时再读；冗长日志只保留经过验证的关键证据。

结果在 EdgeBench 上，SoL-Pi 在 GPT-5.6 Sol 和 Opus 5 上保持接近 Pi 的任务表现，同时减少约 45%–49% 的 Token 流量，API 成本降低约三分之一。并且用 GPT-5.6 Sol 搜出来的 Harness，可以直接迁移到 Opus 5，不需要重新优化。

还有一个细节是最终评测集完全隔离，候选方案冻结后才能进去测试；如果失败，就直接淘汰，结果不会再回流给 Agent 继续针对性修改。这样能尽量避免「为了 benchmark 把 Harness 越改越偏」。

所以这篇工作给的insight是 Harness 自进化未必需要一开始就追求复杂的新架构。

大量价值可能藏在那些每天都在发生的浪费里，重复调用、反复传输、无效上下文和过长日志。

当 AI 开始自己发现并修掉这些系统性浪费，Agent 的「自我改进」也就从能力提升，走到了运行效率这一层。

📎 arxiv: https://t.co/Z4zzJak7NF

reviewedPosts.text:
Noul is a binary classifier!  Binary classifiers (see logistic regression ) output a score, which you can use for decision making 

It’s exactly the same shape of output! 

Don’t get me wrong, I love Jev and think it’s super useful, just not sure we need a new term to describe the output 

Also, people should stop using classifier as an insult.  Classifiers are cool as hell
reviewedPosts.rationale: 基础概念说明，价值有限

Yeah, I don’t think people should dismiss it.  I also see all this stuff on the TL that acts like the classification task is novel and I think the focus is on the wrong parts 

I think the novelty is the speed, cost, portability, accuracy as that makes lots of things possible that may have been infeasible before
